deleteAccount.contactBody: If you can't access your account but want it deleted, contact us at
deleteAccount.onWebBody: Sign in at textstack.app, open the user menu in the top-right corner, choose "Edit profile", then scroll to the "Danger zone" section and select "Delete account". You'll be asked to type DELETE to confirm.
deleteAccount.retentionBody: Deletion happens immediately, in a single transaction — there is no waiting period and no recovery window. Operational records of AI requests are kept as an anonymous cost-and-quality log, with the link to your account removed, so nothing in them identifies you afterwards.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.subheading: Everything you need to know about TextStack.

whatIs.a: TextStack is a reader for people who want to finish the book they keep quitting — dense tech books and papers, or classic literature. Every word you tap gets a contextual explanation tied to the book's domain. Save words to a capped weekly SRS queue. Works on web and mobile, online or offline.

isFree.a: Yes. The full catalog, reader, contextual explanations, translation, SRS flashcards, text-to-speech, and reading statistics are completely free. No credit card required, no hidden limits.

techBooks.q: Do you have programming or tech books?
techBooks.a: The catalog ships with thousands of public-domain classics. MIT/Apache/CC-BY licensed programming books are being added — priority given to Rust, Go, and systems titles. You can also upload your own EPUB or PDF at any time and read it with the full toolkit.

languages.a: You can translate English text into 18+ languages including Spanish, French, German, Ukrainian, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Portuguese, and more. The interface is available in English and Ukrainian.

tapTranslate.a: While reading, simply tap or click any word. You will instantly see the translation in your native language, a dictionary definition, and can hear the pronunciation. No switching apps or copying text.

uploadBooks.q: Can I upload my own books?
uploadBooks.a: Absolutely. Upload EPUB or PDF files and read them with the full TextStack toolkit — translation, flashcards, TTS, and progress tracking.

srsCards.q: How do the SRS flashcards work?
srsCards.a: When you save a word, it becomes an SRS flashcard. The system uses 5 stages — from Recognition to Mastered — spacing reviews so you remember long-term. Smart distractors make each review meaningful.

offline.a: Yes. Download books for offline reading. Your progress, bookmarks, and vocabulary sync automatically when you reconnect.

mobileApp.a: A mobile app for iOS and Android is in active development and coming soon. In the meantime, TextStack works great on mobile browsers.

vsFriends.q: How is TextStack different from Kindle or LingQ?
vsFriends.a: TextStack combines the reading experience of Kindle with the language-learning tools of LingQ — and it is free. Tap-to-translate, SRS flashcards, built-in text-to-speech, offline reading, and detailed statistics, all in one clean reader.

about.seoTitle: About TextStack — open-source reader for developers
about.seoDesc: Open-source reader for developers who want to finish dense English technical books in their native language. Local LLM, AGPL-3.0, self-hostable on a $20 VPS.
about.title: About
about.intro: TextStack is an open-source reader for developers who want to finish dense English technical books in their native language.
about.body1: Tap any term — get a context-aware translation that knows the book's domain. Tap «attention» in an ML chapter and you get «увага (механізм у нейромережах)» in Ukrainian, not the everyday meaning. Words you save feed a capped weekly SRS queue with multiple-choice cards generated by a local Gemma 4 model running on a $20 VPS — no per-user cloud costs.
about.mission1: Real understanding of a technical book comes from finishing it — not from skipping unfamiliar terms or summarizing it away. TextStack is built around that: keep the book in front of you, let the friction (vocabulary, terminology, domain) get out of the way.
about.mission2: Every feature — domain-aware translation, vocabulary builder, spaced repetition, reading stats — exists for one job: get you to the last page of the kind of book you usually quit halfway through.
about.openSource1: TextStack is licensed under GNU AGPL-3.0. The full codebase — .NET 10 backend, React frontend, React Native mobile app — lives at github.com/mrviduus/textstack. You can self-host the entire stack on a $20/month consumer VPS, no GPU required.
about.tech1: Local Gemma 4 model (via Ollama) generates the multiple-choice distractors, vocabulary hints, and book metadata enrichment on your own server — no per-user cloud LLM costs. OpenAI's gpt-4.1-nano handles the translation layer where multilingual quality matters.
about.techStackValue: ASP.NET Core 10 · PostgreSQL 16 · React 19 · React Native (Expo) · Ollama (Gemma 4) · OpenAI gpt-4.1-nano · Docker · Cloudflare Tunnel

creator.heading: The Creator
creator.bio1: I built TextStack because I quit Designing Data-Intensive Applications three times before this. Not because the book was hard — I understood most of what was on the page — but because forty unfamiliar terms broke my flow. Summarizing it away defeated the point. So I built the thing I wanted: tap a term, get the context, keep reading.
creator.bio2: It's an open project I run because I needed it. AGPL-3.0, full codebase on GitHub. If you share the use case or want to contribute, I'd love to hear from you.

mcp.seoTitle: Connect TextStack to your AI assistant (MCP)
mcp.seoDescription: Connect TextStack as an MCP server. Ask your reading library questions, look up highlights, and get explanations from Claude, Cursor, or ChatGPT. Copy-paste install snippets for remote and local clients.
mcp.title: Connect TextStack to your AI assistant
mcp.intro: Ask your reading library questions, look up highlights, save passages, and get explanations — straight from Claude, Cursor, or ChatGPT via the Model Context Protocol.

remote.heading: Remote (recommended)
remote.lead: For Cursor, remote Claude, and ChatGPT: add a custom MCP server / connector pointing at the TextStack endpoint. Transport is Streamable HTTP.
remote.addServer: In your client, choose "add a custom MCP server" (or "connector") and paste the endpoint URL above.
remote.publicTools: Catalog tools (search_books, get_book, get_chapter) work without signing in. Your own uploads need sign-in.
remote.authNote: The first user-scoped call (your highlights or vocabulary) returns a message like "authentication required — open https://textstack.app/device and enter code XXXX-XXXX". Open the device page, sign in, enter the code, then retry.

local.heading: Claude Desktop (local)
local.lead: Add TextStack to your claude_desktop_config.json under mcpServers.
local.nowHint: Requires .NET 10 and the built TextStack.Ai.Mcp.dll. Point the args path at your local copy.
local.toolHint: Install the TextStack.Mcp .NET global tool, then reference its textstack-mcp command directly — no DLL path. Needs .NET 10+; on .NET 10 you can also run it without installing via dnx textstack-mcp.

tools.heading: The 14 tools
tools.lead: What your AI assistant can do once connected:
tools.searchBooks: Search the public book catalog by query.
tools.getBook: Fetch a book's metadata and chapter list by slug.
tools.getChapter: Fetch the full text of a single chapter.
tools.searchMyLibrary: Search the books you uploaded — your own library, not the public catalog (requires sign-in).
tools.getMyBook: Fetch one of your uploaded books: metadata and chapter list (requires sign-in).
tools.getMyChapter: Fetch the full text of one chapter of a book you uploaded (requires sign-in).
tools.saveMyHighlight: Highlight a passage in a book you uploaded (requires sign-in).
tools.listMyBookHighlights: List the highlights already in a book you uploaded (requires sign-in).
tools.saveHighlight: Save a passage to your highlights (requires sign-in).
tools.listMyVocabulary: List your saved vocabulary words (requires sign-in).
tools.askBook: Ask a question about a book and get a cited, grounded answer.
tools.saveInsight: Write a conclusion back into a book — against one chapter, or the whole book (requires sign-in).
tools.getMyInsights: Read back everything already worked out about a book, in reading order (requires sign-in).

steps.heading: Auth in 3 steps
steps.step1: Add the TextStack server to your client (remote endpoint or local config above).
steps.step2: Call a user-scoped tool — the response shows a code and a link to /device.
steps.step3: Open /device, sign in, enter the code, then retry the tool call.

privacy.seoDesc: What TextStack collects, who receives it, and how long we keep it — including the AI features.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what TextStack collects, why, who we send it to, and how long we keep it. It covers the textstack.app website and the TextStack mobile apps.
privacy.scopeHeading: Who we are and what this covers
privacy.scopeBody1: TextStack is a reading platform for language learning. This policy covers the textstack.app website and the TextStack apps for Android and iOS.
privacy.scopeBody2: You can browse the public library and read without an account. Creating an account adds sync, uploads, highlights, vocabulary and the AI features — and means we store data on our servers rather than only on your device.
privacy.collectBody1: Account. Your email address, display name, and a profile picture if you set one. If you sign in with Google or Apple we receive your email, name, profile image URL and a provider identifier. If you use a password, we store a cryptographic hash of it and never the password itself.
privacy.collectBody2: Content you create or upload. The books you upload — both the original file and the text extracted from it — plus your highlights, notes, bookmarks, saved vocabulary and collections. Uploaded books are private to your account.
privacy.collectBody3: Reading activity. Reading sessions (duration, words read, position), progress, goals, streaks and achievements. An earlier version of this policy said this data stayed in your browser. That was wrong: when you are signed in it is stored on our servers and linked to your account, which is what lets it sync across your devices.
privacy.collectBody4: AI interaction data. When you use Book Chat, the tutor, the librarian, Explain or translation, we store a sample of the request and the response — including the passage of the book sent as context, your question, and the model's answer — linked to your account. We use it to investigate quality problems and to monitor what the service costs to run.
privacy.collectBody5: Technical data. IP address, request logs, rate-limiting counters, and device and operating-system type. On the website only, analytics events if you accept analytics cookies.
privacy.collectBody6: Kept only on your device. Theme, fonts, reader layout preferences, and the offline copies of any books you download.
privacy.purposeBody: To run the reading service and sync your library across devices; to produce AI answers, explanations, translations and speech when you ask for them; to prevent abuse and enforce rate limits; and to monitor reliability and what the service costs to operate.
privacy.thirdPartiesIntro: We do not sell your personal information and we do not share it with advertisers or data brokers. We do send data to the providers below, each only as far as a feature you used requires.
privacy.thirdPartiesOpenai: OpenAI. When you use an AI feature, your question and the relevant passage of the book are sent to OpenAI's API (models gpt-4.1 and gpt-4.1-nano) and the answer comes back. Under OpenAI's API terms this content is not used to train their models.
privacy.thirdPartiesTts: Microsoft. Text you ask to be read aloud is sent to the Edge text-to-speech service to be turned into audio.
privacy.thirdPartiesDictionary: Free Dictionary API (dictionaryapi.dev). The single word you look up is sent to fetch its definition and pronunciation. No account information goes with it.
privacy.thirdPartiesAuth: Google and Apple. Only if you choose to sign in with them, and only to verify who you are.
privacy.thirdPartiesEmail: Resend. Receives your email address in order to deliver transactional email such as a password reset.
privacy.thirdPartiesSentry: Sentry. Receives error and performance data from our servers when something fails, which can include details of the failing request.
privacy.thirdPartiesAnalytics: Google Analytics and Ahrefs Analytics. On the textstack.app website only, and only after you accept analytics cookies. The mobile apps contain no analytics.
privacy.thirdPartiesCloudflare: Cloudflare. Carries all traffic to the service as our DNS and network provider.
privacy.thirdPartiesOllama: Some AI work stays with us. The hints and multiple-choice options in vocabulary review are generated by a model running on our own servers and are not sent to anyone.
privacy.aiBody1: They are optional. If you do not use Book Chat, the tutor, the librarian, Explain or translation, nothing is sent to OpenAI.
privacy.aiBody2: AI output can be wrong. Explanations, translations and answers about a book are generated by a language model and should not be relied on as fact.
privacy.aiBody3: We do not train models on your content, and under OpenAI's API terms neither do they. We do keep a sample of prompts and responses, as described above, for quality and cost monitoring.
privacy.aiBody4: If an AI response is offensive or harmful, please report it using the contact address at the bottom of this page.
privacy.cookiesBody1: Essential storage keeps you signed in and remembers your reader preferences. It cannot be switched off without breaking the service.
privacy.cookiesBody2: The website asks for your consent before loading Google Analytics and Ahrefs Analytics. Analytics stays off until you accept, and you can decline. We use no advertising cookies, and the mobile apps ship no analytics or advertising SDKs at all.
privacy.securityBody: Data travels over HTTPS and is stored on servers we control. Books you upload are private to your account. Access to production systems is limited to the operator.
privacy.retentionBody1: Account data and the content you create are kept until you delete them, or until you delete your account.
privacy.retentionBody2: Generated speech and cached AI explanations are deleted after 30 days.
privacy.retentionBody3: AI interaction records are kept indefinitely — they are the operational record of what the service did and what it cost. When you delete your account, the link between those records and you is removed and they remain only as anonymous entries.
privacy.rightsHeading: Your rights, and how to use them
privacy.rightsBody1: You can access and export your data, correct it, or delete it. Deleting your account is immediate and irreversible: the account, uploaded books, highlights, notes, vocabulary, reading history and stored files are removed in a single transaction.
privacy.rightsBody2: In the app: open the Profile tab, scroll to Delete account, and confirm. On the website: sign in, open the user menu, choose Edit profile, then use the Danger zone. You can also start a deletion request without signing in from the page below.
privacy.childrenBody: TextStack is not directed to children under 13 and we do not knowingly collect their personal information. If you believe a child has created an account, contact us and we will remove it.
privacy.transfersBody: Several of the providers above — OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, Apple, Resend, Sentry and Cloudflare — process data in the United States and elsewhere. Using the features that depend on them transfers your data there.
privacy.changesBody: If this policy changes materially we will update the date at the top, and for significant changes we will say so in the app or on the site. This version replaces an earlier one that understated both what we store and who receives it.
privacy.contactBody: Questions about this policy, or a request about your data? Reach out at

terms.aiBody1: TextStack includes features powered by large language models: Book Chat, the tutor, the librarian, Explain, and translation. Their output is generated, not verified, and can be wrong, incomplete or misleading. Do not rely on it as fact, and do not rely on it for advice of any kind.
terms.aiBody2: Using these features sends the text you selected or asked about, together with the surrounding passage, to our AI providers. See the Privacy Policy for who receives it and what is stored. If a response is offensive or harmful, report it to the contact address below and we will look into it.

dmca.seoDesc: How to submit a DMCA takedown notice for content hosted on TextStack Reader. Full process, requirements, and contact.
dmca.title: DMCA Takedown Policy
dmca.intro: TextStack Reader respects copyright. If you believe your work has been copied and made available on this site in a way that infringes your copyright, use the process below to request removal.
dmca.howBody: To file a valid takedown notice under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), include all of the following in a single email:
dmca.req1: A description of the copyrighted work you claim has been infringed.
dmca.req2: The exact URL(s) on this site where the allegedly infringing material is located.
dmca.req3: Your full legal name, mailing address, phone number, and email address.
dmca.req4: A statement that you have a good-faith belief the disputed use is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law.
dmca.req5: A statement, under penalty of perjury, that the information in the notice is accurate and that you are the owner or authorized to act on behalf of the owner.
dmca.sendBody: Send the complete notice to our designated agent at
dmca.sendNote: Incomplete notices will not be processed. We may share your notice (including contact details) with the user who uploaded the disputed content.
dmca.processBody1: Once we receive a valid notice, we will act expeditiously to remove or disable access to the material and notify the uploader.
dmca.processBody2: We typically respond within a few business days. Complex claims may take longer.
dmca.counterBody: If you believe your content was removed in error, you may submit a counter-notice to the same address. Include your contact details, identify the removed material, state under penalty of perjury that the removal was a mistake or misidentification, and consent to the jurisdiction of a US federal court (or, if outside the US, your local equivalent).
dmca.repeatBody: We terminate accounts of users who repeatedly upload infringing material.
dmca.misuseBody: Under Section 512(f) of the DMCA, anyone who knowingly materially misrepresents that material is infringing (or was removed by mistake) may be liable for damages. Please submit notices in good faith.
